Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Quick update from procurement — there is an internal vendor on-boarding and security review that just landed on our side. Legal needs a short review of your SOC2 evidence and our procurement lead flagged a third-party questionnaire that we only just received.

Realistically, we cannot hit the June 30 close anymore. Procurement asks for a 2–3 week buffer to finish the security paperwork and PO approvals. I know this complicates your internal cadence — apologies for the late notice.

Could you send a concrete MAP update with gating criteria so my team can sign off quicker? Also, any temporary configuration that allows a staged pilot (restricted data subset) would help us progress while the full onboarding completes.

Thanks,
Camille Park
Director, Vendor Programs
Veridian Health

From: jonas_weber@example.com <jonas_weber@example.com>

Camille — thanks for the heads up and the procurement note.

We can propose three containment options to minimize risk to the close and let you finish onboarding:

1) Short buffer + gated acceptance (preferred) — push close by 14 days, maintain current commercial terms, acceptance gated on receipt of SOC2 evidence + signed PO.
2) Staged pilot (escape hatch) — allow a constrained pilot (up to 5 users, no PHI export) effective immediately under a temporary Data Processing Addendum; full go-live contingent on completed questionnaire.
3) Credit + extension — 10% credit if customer needs >30 day extension (exec approval required).

I'm attaching an updated MAP (MAP_v4.xlsx) that documents the gating checkpoints, owners, and dates for each option. Ben and Marissa — can you weigh in on the credit/exec path if procurement insists on longer lead time?

Camille — can procurement confirm who has final PO sign authority and the expected timeline for the questionnaire? That will let us choose the path that minimizes risk to both sides.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0147

Team — adding recommended mitigation language for exec approval. Draft below that I can turn into a short proposal PDF if we agree: 

- Risk entry: Close slip risk — procurement onboarding delay (Veridian). Impact: potential loss of end-of-quarter ARR recognition; mitigation: staged pilot + temporary terms or committed credit.
- Proposed mitigations:
  * Short buffer (14 days) with unchanged commercials.
  * Staged pilot under a temporary DPA (no PHI export; limited accounts).
  * Credit alternative: 10% credit applied to first invoice if close is >30 days delayed.
- Ask: Sales leadership approval for credit (up to 10%) and CS to prepare pilot onboarding checklist.
- Evidence: attach SOC2 extract we can share immediately to speed review.

I've attached a quick procurement-bridge-proposal.pdf and the SOC2-evidence-extract.pdf. If Neha can approve routing the 10% credit as a one-time sales concession, we can offer a dual-path (pilot + credit) to reduce churn risk.

— Ben

Sr. Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

Camille — thanks for the quick turn. Based on procurement's note and our internal options, proposed path forward (please confirm):

1) Immediate: offer staged pilot (escape hatch) — Redwood provides a constrained pilot environment (5 users, no external exports) under a temporary DPA. Pilot contract to be executed this week.
2) Parallel: Redwood provides SOC2 evidence extract (attached) and a short checklist for Veridian security to accelerate review.
3) Contingency: if questionnaire push extends beyond July 12, Redwood will apply an agreed credit up to 10% on the first invoice OR accept a 14-day formal extension without penalty (your preference).

We've updated the MAP (MAP_v4.xlsx) with explicit gates and rollback steps and linked the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/VER-2026-2791. Ben/Marissa/Neha — please confirm approval for the credit contingency so I can include the concession in the pilot offer.

Camille — if you can confirm by Thursday EOD (June 24) we'll target a pilot start on June 28, which preserves most of the quarter momentum. If you need the exec escalation pack instead, we'll prepare the short pack and route to S. Ellison.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

— Jonas
